newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria refinery eases fuel crisis, raises output.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria refinery eases fuel crisis, raises output.

text.p: Bulgaria's biggest oil refinery, Neftochim, has increased its fuel distribution, easing a month-long fuel crisis, a plant spokeswoman said on Wednesday.

Tatyana Hadzhieva said Neftochim had raised daily distribution volumes of diesel for the domestic market to more than 3,500 tonnes from some 1,000 tonnes last month and customers could now supply as much as they needed.
The plant will continue to distribute 1,300 tonnes of petrol per day, she said.

The Bourgas refinery, which lacked cash to buy crude, will start refining 14,000 tonnes of crude per day by the end of the week up from 12,000 tonnes last week, still down from 22,000 tonnes in December.

The interim government, which inherited crippling fuel shortages when it took office in mid-February, raised petrol prices twice last month by up to 178 percent and by up to 10 percent in line with the lev/dollar exchange rate and inflation.
It also banned fuel exports until April 30 and troops enforced border controls in a bid to curb oil smuggling to neighbouring countries where prices are higher.

Neftochim, which owes millions of dollars to its crude suppliers, expects six tankers of about 70,000 tonnes of Russian crude in March supplied by its joint venture with Russia's Rosneft, Rosbulneft, and by a private firm Yukos Bulgaria.
Last month Neftochim agreed a $50-million credit with France's Paribas Bank branch in Geneva.
The refinery now has 101,000 tonnes of crude on stock.
The interim government said it planned Neftochim's partial privatisation, but has not given yet any further details.
